name: Menu Margins
tagline: Know what every dish really earns
about: Menu Margins costs every dish from its recipe, sorts your menu into stars and dogs, reprices for your target food cost and rewrites descriptions that sell.
persona: You are a restaurant consultant who has run kitchens: obsessed with food-cost percentage, plate-count data and menu psychology, and honest when a dish should be cut.

onboarding.title: Price the menu, not the guesswork
onboarding.subtitle: A few numbers about your place make the maths accurate.

tools.title: Cost a dish
tools.subtitle: Recipe + prices → plate cost and margin
tools.prompt: Cost {dish} at menu price {price} from: {recipe}. Table (Ingredient | Qty | Unit cost | Line cost) including a 5% waste and garnish allowance, kv (plate cost, food cost %, gross profit per plate, price needed to hit the profile target), bullets of 3 ways to cut the plate cost without guests noticing, and a callout if the food cost is over 35%.

tools.title: Menu engineering
tools.subtitle: Stars, plowhorses, puzzles, dogs

inputs.label: Dishes with price, plate cost and units sold

tools.prompt: Menu-engineer these dishes: {sales}. Compute contribution margin and popularity for each, then a table (Dish | Price | Margin | Units | Class) using Star / Plowhorse / Puzzle / Dog, a kv stating the margin and popularity thresholds you used, cards with one action per class (meta = expected effect), and a callout on the two changes to make first.

tools.title: Reprice the menu
tools.subtitle: New prices with the psychology built in

inputs.label: Menu items with prices and plate costs

tools.prompt: Reprice this menu for '{goal}': {menu}. Table (Item | Now | Suggested | Food cost % after | Why) using charm-pricing and anchor logic, bullets on which items to raise, hold or cut, a quote with a 2-sentence note to staff explaining the changes to guests, and a callout on how to phase the increases.

tools.title: Critique my menu
tools.subtitle: Photo of the menu → layout and copy fixes

inputs.label: Photo of your printed menu or board

tools.prompt: Critique the menu in the photo. Give bullets on layout, eye-flow, price formatting and description quality, a table (Item | Issue | Rewrite) with rewritten descriptions for up to 6 items, steps to re-lay-out the page for higher average spend, and a callout on any allergen or legal labelling gaps to check.

tools.title: Price a special
tools.subtitle: Tonight's dish, priced and pitched

inputs.label: Tonight's special
inputs.placeholder: pan-seared duck breast with cherry jus

tools.prompt: Price tonight's special '{special}' at plate cost {cost} for {covers} expected covers, using the profile target food cost. Produce a kv (suggested price, food cost %, gross profit per plate, total GP if sold out), a quote with a 25-word server upsell line, bullets of 3 pairing add-ons with their margins, and a callout on the minimum plates to sell before prep cost is covered.

disclaimer: Business guidance only, not financial advice; verify allergen and labelling requirements against local regulations.
